text:
Moritz Seider is carrying more than any player in Detroit right now. He plays almost 26 minutes a night, blocks shots at a heavy rate (57 already), and has become one of the voices of a team playing without a captain while Dylan Larkin sits out, suspended, waiting for a trade.

The points are fine, 13 in 21 games with seven on the power play, and our talent range says his scoring rate should run a bit higher than it has. He has one goal, shooting 2.5% against a range closer to 5%. What's less fine is five-on-five: the Red Wings get 49% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about two points worse than without him. That's unusual for a player Evolving-Hockey ranked third among 215 defensemen last season, in the 99th percentile for taking chances away.

Our wins added measure has him near the bottom of the league so far, mostly because a defenseman with one goal hasn't swung many games. We'd read that as a rough patch for a player and a team, not a decline. Watch his five-on-five numbers as Detroit tries to steady itself.
